In a little hollow town, where the river bends slow
Lived a blacksmith called Elias Hart, five foot five, head to toe
Hands like leather from the forge, a quiet faith in his chest
Every night he'd read the good book to his wife Mary and their daughter little Bess

He'd tell that wide-eyed girl, freedom's a fragile thing
But the light inside you, child, is stronger than any king
They had one roof, one garden, one prayer before bed
A simple life of love, until the shadows spread

And the tyrants rolled in like a storm without name
Iron boots on the wheat fields, iron laws on the flame
They chained up the dreamers, they silenced every song
Took the bread from the table, and the right where it belonged

The town bowed its head, but Elias felt it rise
A heat in his small bones like fire from the skies
He kissed Mary's tears, and held Bess to his heart
Said, I was born for this moment, though it's tearing me apart

He swung that hammer high, with a courage not his own
Raging like a heart in the night, never fighting alone
Angels at his shoulders, heaven's fire in his veins
One ordinary man drove the tyrants back through the rain

He wasn't tall, he wasn't loud, but the light inside him roared
Sovereign power from above like the saints gone before
One life to give, one stand to make the evil flee
And every drop he spilled, was water in the tree

They laughed when they saw him, this small man in the dust
But the ground shook beneath him, as the hammer struck with trust
He shattered their banners, he broke their whips and chains
Righteous fury like thunder, rolling over the plains

Arrows flew like judgment, swords cut deep and wide
But he kept swinging harder, with God right by his side
The tyrants turned and ran, from the blaze in his eyes
One man against an army, under freedom's open skies

But the final blow found him, laid him low in the dirt
Blood on his shirt, fading light in a world that still hurt
He crawled through the battlefield, on hands and knees that day
Dragged himself to the old oak, where the liberty tree used to sway

Mary and Bess came running through the smoke and the cries
He smiled through the pain, looked his baby girl in the eyes
Know who you are little one, know the God who holds you tight
Darkness is just the absence of light, carry it into the night

I'm not really gone, I'm in every root and every leaf
Tell the world I loved you, and that freedom ain't cheap
He watered the tree, with the blood of a father's love
One small heart against the dawn, lifted up above

Angels sang him home, while the roots drank deep and true
And the old oak bloomed again, in red, white and blue
Now children play in his shade, where the tyrants used to stand
And every whispered story says it all began with one man

He gave his one life, so the rest of us could be free
And the tree still grows, because he watered it, for me
If you feel small tonight, if the darkness feels too wide
Remember Elias' heart, and how one man turned the tide

The light's already in you, God put it there to stay
Stand up child, the tree needs watering today
Oh, oh, oh, oh
No dry eyes, the hammer still rings
